svg.title: C13 / HORIZON RING ATLAS engineering mission profile
svg.desc: C13, HORIZON RING ATLAS. Original project: Characterizing the Images of Black Hole Shadows. Session C: Astronomy & Space Physics. Scientific question: Which ring diameter, width, asymmetry, and central-depression measures remain stable across imaging methods, calibration choices, and sparse baseline coverage? Testable hypothesis: Direct fitting of visibility-domain geometric models combined with independent image reconstructions will yield more defensible geometry than measuring a single favored reconstructed image.. svg.text: Characterizing the Images of Black Hole Shadows
No project observations acquired · specified cases await execution · shared demonstrations are separately labeled
Measure robust geometric features of black-hole emission-ring images through
the interferometric observation process. Use public Event Horizon Telescope
visibilities and released imaging products to distinguish data-supported
ring geometry from regularization choices. The apparent emission ring and
central brightness depression are related to strong-field lensing but are
not identical to an isolated, directly photographed event horizon.
Which ring diameter, width, asymmetry, and central-depression measures
remain stable across imaging methods, calibration choices, and sparse
TESTABLE HYPOTHESIS / NOT AN OBSERVED RESULT
Direct fitting of visibility-domain geometric models combined with
independent image reconstructions will yield more defensible geometry than
measuring a single favored reconstructed image.
Use visibility and closure likelihoods appropriate to their signal-to-noise
Include source variability and interstellar scattering where applicable; do
not assume M87 and Sgr A have identical observation models.
VALIDITY LIMITS / THE CLAIM STOPS HERE
Sparse Fourier coverage can imprint structure, and emission physics changes
the relationship between ring size and photon orbit. Image pixels are
strongly correlated; treating every pixel as an independent measurement
COUNTS OF RECORDS · NO COMPLETION SCORES
TRACEABILITY / IDs THAT STAY WITH THE WORK
Execution evidence is required before case closure.
References are pointers; archive acquisition is separate.
A question becomes a model. A model earns evidence.
NASA-inspired mission names are creative identifiers. This profile describes research design; it claims no NASA approval or flight qualification.
Original titles are preserved. Data pointers and citations do not establish that the original teams’ observations have been acquired.
